question: Should a family doctor be allowed to remove patients from the practice list because they refuse childhood vaccines?
answer: An unvaccinated child in the waiting room exposes newborns and chemotherapy patients to measles. A doctor who has tried repeatedly and failed should be free to end a relationship built on distrust. The American Academy of Pediatrics said in 2016 that dismissal can be acceptable, after repeated counselling, as a last resort.
move: What decides it is whether a doctor's leverage lies in the threat or the relationship.
ask: When I need someone to change, do I use pressure or the relationship?
counterpoint: Dismissed families do not get vaccinated; they gather in the few practices that will take them, or drift away from medicine, and outbreaks follow such clusters. Many hesitant parents do vaccinate after continued conversations, sometimes years later, and only a doctor they still see can hold them. Dismissal also cuts siblings off from check-ups and ordinary care.
reference: Edwards & Hackell, Countering Vaccine Hesitancy, Pediatrics, 2016
